title: Karnataka REAT: Plan Attached to Sale Deed Is Not Allottee Consent for Added Commercial Block
case_name: Amit Garg v. SJR Prime Corporation Pvt. Ltd.
citation: Appeal No. K-REAT 64 of 2026, decided 27 October 2026
card_summary: The Karnataka Real Estate Appellate Tribunal set aside a K-RERA order letting SJR Prime Corporation add a commercial block to its Palazza City project. The original plan had no such block; the revised one put it on land meant for a park, and the developer relied only on a general consent clause in the sale deeds. This breached Section 14 of RERA, which needs written consent from two-thirds of allottees.
card_tip: A revised plan merely attached to a sale deed, or a general consent clause in it, does not satisfy Section 14's requirement of specific, written, two-thirds allottee consent before a structural change.
verification_notes: Confirmed by two independent reports (LiveLawBiz, Oquilia) and the LiveLawBiz RERA weekly digest, consistent on parties, project, date and relief; tribunal order itself not accessed.
